summary: Discovery call to understand Emerald's current vector search stack, throughput and latency targets, hybrid search needs (BM25 + ANN + rerank), dimensionality questions, and security/compliance constraints. Redwood AE+SE covered hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, integration patterns with vector DBs, and a proposed 4-week POC + benchmark plan.
topics: vector DB integration patterns (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE. we've got James from SE here. um quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: Hi I'm Lena, head of search at Emerald, Arjun's on the ML team, Diane from security will listen in.
[00:14] James: Hey all, James Chen, infra/latency nerd.
[00:18] Arjun: Arjun Rao, ML Eng, I'll lead the POC.
[00:22] Diane: Diane Park, security lead.
[00:25] Maya: Thanks. Goal for today is to understand your current vector search infra, throughput, and requirements for reranking and then talk about Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Sound good?
[00:33] Lena: Yep. quick context — we run a multi-tenant ecommerce site search. currently using Elastic with dense-vector plugin + a small Pinecone index for some experiments. main complaints: p99 latency spikes during sales, and re-ranking is expensive since our cross-encoder is heavy.
[00:48] Maya: Got it. can you give numbers — qps, index size, dims?
[00:52] Arjun: Sure. traffic baseline 200 qps search queries, spikes to ~1k during promos. docs ~12M, our passage vectors are 1536 dims using OpenAI embeddings right now, average vector per doc 1.2 (we store title+snippet). we keep a hybrid approach: BM25 for recall then ANN for rerank candidates, then cross-encoder re-rank on top 10.
[01:12] James: That's helpful. so your big cost is the 10 cross-encoder runs per query and the peak qps. are you running batching for cross-encoder?
[01:18] Arjun: minimal batching; latency constraint is tight. p95 target is <120ms end-to-end, p99 <300ms (user facing). cross-encoder adds 80-200ms depending on hardware.
[01:28] Maya: Understood. Redwood can help two ways: reduce token/compute cost for rerank using efficient rerank models or offload reranker to dedicated inference to hit latency SLOs, and improve ANN throughput using vector servers or integrated vector DBs.
[01:38] Lena: We care about integration - we don't want to rip and replace Pinecone right away. can Redwood sit in front and call Pinecone, or do you recommend moving indexes?
[01:46] James: You can do both. common pattern: Redwood serves embeddings and rerank models, and sits between your app and vector DB. two options — 1) Redwood-hosted API issues embeddings + rerank responses and you keep Pinecone for ANN where Redwood calls Pinecone for KNN and re-ranks candidates; 2) move to dedicated Redwood + local vector DB (Milvus/Weaviate) colocated for lower latency and higher throughput.
[02:08] Diane: For option 2 we need VPC, KMS and SOC2 info. can you share compliance docs?
[02:14] Maya: Yes, we'll send SOC2 and our security whitepaper. for private deployments we support customer-managed VPC, HSM/KMS integrations, audit logs and single-tenant control plane. we'll include the SAML/SSO options.
[02:24] Arjun: On embeddings dimensionality — is 1536 overkill? would moving to 512 vector dims speed up ANN and rerank without losing quality?
[02:31] James: There's a tradeoff. lower dims reduce ANN memory and speed up queries, but retrieval quality can drop. we've seen for e-commerce that a 512-d distilled embedding can get close for product search, especially if you use hybrid signals (title BM25 + vector). recommended experiment: try 512 vs 1536 on a holdout set and measure recall@k and rerank quality. our benchmark kit can run that.
[02:51] Lena: How about rerank model size — can you do pairwise light models instead of cross-encoder full BERT?
[02:56] James: Yes — pairwise dot-product or lightweight cross-encoders (distilled) reduce latency. also Redwood supports batching, multi-request merging and kv cache for conversational flows; for reranking we can use sequence-level caching for repeated queries. small tradeoff vs accuracy.
[03:12] Arjun: We also care about ANN index consistency and replication. during spikes we saw slowdowns in Pinecone region failover. would Dedicated give us more predictable throughput?
[03:20] Maya: Dedicated pools are reserved GPU capacity with autoscaling and burst policies. you get predictable throughput and can colocate vector DBs for lower network hops. Hosted is easier to get started but can have noisy neighbor if you need strict SLOs at scale. Private on-prem is possible too if you need full control.
[03:36] Diane: For Private (on-prem) do you manage software updates or is it fully customer-controlled? any remote agents?
[03:42] James: Private deployments are customer-controlled with an optional Redwood control plane. updates can be scheduled; we don't run arbitrary remote code in your network. for enterprise we do managed ops agreements.
[03:51] Lena: Cost — any back-of-envelope TCO differences between hosted and dedicated for our scale (12M docs, 200->1k qps spikes)?
[03:58] Maya: We'll send a TCO worksheet but quick: hosted costs scale with qps and token usage (per-embedding + per-rerank). Dedicated is capacity commit monthly — higher baseline but lower per-unit cost at high sustained qps and better latency. Private adds license + infra ops.
[04:12] Arjun: On integration — if we keep Pinecone, latencies between Redwood and Pinecone matter. do you support colocated connectors / prefer vector DB in same region?
[04:20] James: Yes colocating in same region/zone is recommended. Redwood can run in region close to your vector DB or we can run dedicated instances in your VPC to reduce network hops. for benchmarks, we'll test 3 architectures: hosted->Pinecone remote, hosted->Pinecone same region, dedicated colocated with open-source vector DB.
[04:37] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:40] Maya: Quick Q — what are your p99/throughput budget constraints from business?
[04:43] Lena: p99 <300ms as mentioned and cost per search must be under $0.003 at baseline (ballpark).
[04:49] James: ok we'll include approximate per-search cost numbers based on embedding dims and reranker compute.
[04:55] Arjun: For rerank — we want to explore two-stage where ANN returns top 100 then a small cross-encoder re-ranks top 10 vs returning top 20 and re-ranking top 20. tradeoffs?
[05:04] James: Returning top 100 increases candidate recall but more rerank compute if you rerank all; better pattern: ANN top 100 then light re-ranker on top 20. Also you can use hybrid scoring: BM25 boost then ANN score then rerank. we'll model cost vs quality in the benchmark.
[05:18] Lena: Any pitfalls with dimensionality conversion? we have embeddings generated from OpenAI — do we need to re-embed?
[05:24] James: You can either distill to lower-dim embeddings (model-internal projection) or re-run a smaller embedder. sometimes distillation yields slight loss but is faster. we'll test both.
[05:34] Diane: Security questions — where are embeddings stored, retention, encryption at rest?
[05:39] Maya: Hosted: we encrypt at rest and in transit, SOC2, optional customer KMS with enterprise. Dedicated: data isolated per-tenant and you can bring your KMS. Private: fully within your control. we'll attach the compliance pack and KMS integration docs.
[05:52] Arjun: For the POC/benchmark — what metrics do you capture?
[05:55] James: Latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (qps), CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, recall@k, MRR, cost per query, and memory/IO for vector DB. Our harness can run sustained qps, spike tests, and cold vs warm cache runs.
[06:10] Lena: Good. timeframe? we want a POC before end of month.
[06:14] Maya: Proposed 4-week POC: week 1 dataset ingestion & baseline; week 2 run hosted->Pinecone tests; week 3 dedicated colocated tests; week 4 analyze and TCO. quick win demo in 7-10 days.
[06:25] Diane: Need security review in week 2.
[06:28] Maya: We'll schedule that.
[06:30] Arjun: A couple technical nitty gritty — what about dimensionality in the vector DB index config, IVF/HNSW settings? any recommended defaults?
[06:36] James: For HNSW, tune efConstruction and efSearch; for high throughput prefer HNSW with PQ/OPQ quantization if memory is a concern. we often recommend efSearch ~200 for high recall, efConstruction tuned during batch build. For IVF, tune nlist relative to dataset size. our benchmark will sweep those.
[06:52] Speaker 2: (laugh)
[06:55] Maya: Also mention rerank models: lightweight cross-encoders (distil) vs bi-encoder + cross-encoder combo. cost/latency different.
[07:03] Arjun: What about caching — can Redwood cache intermediate candidates or reranker outputs?
[07:08] James: Yes, prefix & KV caching for conversational flows and result-level caching for identical queries; you can cache reranker outputs for popular queries. Redwood supports TTLs and cache invalidation hooks. note cache can be warmed to reduce cold p99.
[07:20] Lena: Ok, decision factors for us: minimal change to infra, meet p99 SLO during spikes, and reduce per-search cost.
[07:28] Maya: Agreed. we'll run the three-arch benchmark and deliver a recommendation.
[07:32] Arjun: Anything else?
[07:34] Diane: please include data residency notes — EU customers require no data leaving region.
[07:39] Maya: noted; we'll include region-specific hosting options.
[07:42] --[short silence]--
[07:49] James: I'll enumerate the baseline configs we'll test in the plan: dims {1536,512}, rerank {heavy cross-encoder, distilled cross-encoder, pairwise}, vector DB {Pinecone remote, Pinecone same-region, Milvus colocated}, batch sizes, efSearch sweep.
[08:04] Lena: Great. can you share example cost numbers for rerank on A100 vs rtx5000?
[08:10] James: we'll include sample per-inference ms & cost for common GPUs. rough numbers now: A100 faster and more cost-efficient at scale; small GPUs ok for low qps but not for spikes.
[08:20] Arjun: We sometimes do on-the-fly re-ranking only for a subset of queries (e.g. high value). can Redwood route based on policy?
[08:26] Maya: Yes, routing policies supported — latent sensitive vs cheap path. you can set thresholds for model tiering and fallback policies.
[08:33] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[08:36] Diane: On audit logs: do you provide per-request audit trails including model version and inputs?
[08:41] Maya: Yes, per-request logs, model versioning, and we can redact sensitive fields. logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[08:47] Arjun: For the benchmark harness, how do we measure quality for rerank? we use NDCG/MRR ground truth.
[08:52] James: We'll measure NDCG@10 and MRR, plus human eval for a small sample if you want.
[08:58] Lena: Ok let's recap next steps.
[09:01] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing and compliance docs, James will send benchmark kit and config, Arjun will upload dataset, Diane to confirm compliance Qs, schedule security review. POC plan 4 weeks with three architecture tests.
[09:18] Lena: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:21] Maya: Thanks all.
[09:23] --call ends--
